status.description: Status is the current status of the Service.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Service represents a protected upstream resource (e.g. a web application, an API, an SSH server, a database, a Kubernetes cluster, etc...) inside the Cluster. A Service is implemented by Vigil, an identity-aware proxy (IaP) that understands the application-layer protocol of the upstream and provides access control, secretless access, dynamic configuration as well as application-layer visibility and access logging. Every Service belongs to a single Namespace and has the private FQDN `<SERVICE>.<NAMESPACE>.local.<DOMAIN>` and, when publicly exposed, the public FQDN `<SERVICE>.<NAMESPACE>.<DOMAIN>`.

match.description: Match contains a single CEL expression

all.description: All acts as a logical AND operator on its list of CEL expressions

any.description: Any acts as a logical OR operator on its list of CEL expressions

not.description: Not acts as a logical NOT operator of a single CEL expression

none.description: None acts as a logical NOR operator on its list of CEL expressions (i.e. none of the expressions matches)

opa.description: OPA contains an OPA (Open Policy Agent) Rego script

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.title: Condition
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.description: Condition is a policy-as-code expression that is evaluated against the request context. It is used by the Policy rules, the Service dynamic configuration rules, the HTTP Plugins as well as by the IdentityProvider rules.

of.description: Of is the list of the Conditions that must all match

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.All.title: All
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.All.description: All acts as a logical AND operator on its list of Conditions

of.description: Of is the list of the Conditions of which at least one must match

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.Any.title: Any
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.Any.description: Any acts as a logical OR operator on its list of Conditions

of.description: Of is the list of the Conditions of which none must match

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.None.title: None
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.None.description: None acts as a logical NOR operator on its list of Conditions

inline.description: Inline is the OPA Rego script directly provided as a string

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.OPA.title: OPA
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Condition.OPA.description: OPA evaluates the Condition via an Open Policy Agent Rego script

name.description: Name is the name of the inline Policy

octelium.api.main.core.v1.InlinePolicy.title: Inline Policy
octelium.api.main.core.v1.InlinePolicy.description: InlinePolicy is a Policy that is defined inline within the resource that attaches it instead of being created as a standalone Policy resource.

rules.description: Rules is the list of Policy rules

enforcementRules.description: EnforcementRules is the list of enforcement rules that are typically used as a precondition for using the Policy rules. You can simply extract your shared conditions from your rules and write them instead inside enforcementRules for better performance and readability

attrs.description: Attrs is a map of user-defined attributes that can be reused inside the Policy rules. It is strongly recommended to stick to camelCase in order to be conformant with Octelium's API naming conventions.

isDisabled.description: IsDisabled disables (i.e. deactivates) the Policy. You can use this to temporarily disable enforcing the Policy altogether instead of having to delete it or de-attach it from the different Resources attaching it.

condition.description: Condition is the enforcement rule's Condition

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: Effect is the decision of the EnforcementRule once its Condition matches

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Policy.Spec.En.title: Enforcement Rule
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Policy.Spec.En.description: EnforcementRule is a pre-condition that decides whether the Policy is evaluated at all. If no EnforcementRule matches, or if the list of EnforcementRules is empty, then the Policy is enforced. ENFORCE rules always override IGNORE rules in the same way that DENY rules override ALLOW rules.

name.description: Name is an optional name for the rule. It is currently useful in Logs to understand which rule triggered the Policy.

condition.description: Condition is the rule's Condition that must match in order for the rule, and subsequently the Policy as whole, to match

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: Effect is the decision of the Rule once its Condition matches

priority.description: Priority is an integer that sets the rule priority level. The lower the number, the higher the priority. Currently the range of numbers is between -4 (i.e. the highest priority) and 4 (i.e. the lowest priority).

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Policy.Spec.Ru.title: Rule
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Policy.Spec.Ru.description: Rule is a single access control rule of the Policy

port.description: Port is the port number used by the listener. If not set, Octelium will try to assume the number from the backend URL. (e.g. if the backend's URL scheme is `http` then the port number is 80).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Mode is the application-layer protocol understood by the proxy implementing the Service

config.description: Config sets the listener's application-layer specific options.

dynamicConfig.description: DynamicConfig sets the dynamic configuration options. DynamicConfig can simply dynamically override the global/static Service configuration via programmable CEL rules that take identity and context into account.

isTLS.description: IsTLS enables TLS for the listener using its Namespace certificate (i.e. You have to enable TLS at the Namespace level in order to enable this field).

isPublic.description: IsPublic enables the client-less public "BeyondCorp" mode access for the Service. Only works for HTTP-based Service modes for now.

isAnonymous.description: IsAnonymous turns a publicly exposed HTTP-based Service into an anonymously exposed Service that can be anonymously accessed publicly. In other words, this turns off authentication and authorization for the Service. This requires the isPublic field to be enabled too. Refer to the docs for more.

deployment.description: Deployment sets the Service's underlying deployment configurations.

isDisabled.description: IsDisabled disables the Service. Simply the Service stops accepting requests altogether as if it is not running.

attrs.description: Attrs is a map of user-defined attributes, mostly used in authorization rules. It is strongly recommended to stick to camelCase in order to be conformant with Octelium's API naming conventions.

region.description: Region explicitly sets the Region name in which the Service is deployed. By default, a Service is deployed in the "default" Region.

policies.description: Policies is the list of standalone Policies

inlinePolicies.description: InlinePolicies is the list of inline Policies

enableAnonymous.description: EnableAnonymous enables authorization for anonymous Services (i.e. Services whose isAnonymous field is enabled). By default, an anonymous Service enforces no authorization at all. Once enabled, the Policies of the Service are evaluated for the anonymous requests and, as it is the case with the authenticated authorization, a request that matches no rule is denied.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.A.title: Authorization
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.A.description: Authorization sets the Policies that are applied to the Service

name.description: Name is a unique name the describes the Config. Only needed for Configs described within the DynamicConfig. The default Config is assumed to have the name "default".

clientCertificate.description: ClientCertificate sets mTLS-related configuration (i.e. the client x509 certificate chain and its corresponding private key) to authenticate to an upstream that requires mTLS. This is unused for certain modes such as SSH since it does not use mTLS.

upstream.description: Upstream is the Service detailed upstream information. Only one of the URL or Upstream must be set.

parent.description: Parent is the name of the parent configuration

tls.description: TLS sets the TLS client-side configuration used by the Service to connect to an upstream that is listening over TLS.

mcp.description: MCP sets Model Context Protocol-specific configuration

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Config
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Config is the Service configuration. It contains the upstream information as well as the configuration that is specific to the application-layer protocol used by the Service.

trustedCAs.description: TrustedCAs is the list of the PEM-encoded root certificate authorities that are trusted to verify the upstream's certificate.

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the PEM representations of both the client certificate chain and its corresponding private key

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Client Certificate
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: ClientCertificate sets the x509 client certificate used to authenticate to an upstream that requires mTLS

header.description: Header sets request and response header manipulation options

path.description: Path sets the request path options

cors.description: CORS sets the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)-specific options. Read more at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers.

isUpstreamHTTP2.description: IsUpstreamHTTP2 sets HTTP connections to the upstream to HTTP/2. Not enabled by default.

listenHTTP2.description: ListenHTTP2 sets the Service to listen to HTTP 2.0 connections. This is only enabled by default for Services using TLS. This field has to be enabled in the in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

enableRequestBuffering.description: EnableRequestBuffering buffers the entire request body before sending it to the upstream. This can be used to check the request body content for access control and dynamic configuration. This means that it has to be enabled in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

plugins.description: Plugins is the list of plugins

visibility.description: Visibility sets the visibility/access logging specific options

retry.description: Retry sets the retrying of the failed upstream requests

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: HTTP
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: HTTP sets the HTTP-specific configuration. It is used by every HTTP-based Service mode (i.e. HTTP, WEB and GRPC).

custom.description: Custom sets authentication inside custom header

oauth2ClientCredentials.description: OAuth2ClientCredentials sets OAuth2 client credentials authentication flow details

sigv4.description: Sigv4 sets the AWS signature v4 authentication details

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Auth
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Auth sets the application-layer credentials that are injected by the Service on-the-fly to authenticate to the upstream. This provides secretless access where the credentials are never shared with the Users.

username.description: Username is the username value of HTTP basic authentication

password.description: Password is the password value of HTTP basic authentication

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Basic
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Basic is the HTTP basic authentication credentials

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the Password

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Password
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Password is the password value of HTTP basic authentication

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the bearer token

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Bearer
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Bearer is the bearer token that is set in the `Authorization` request header

header.description: Header is the name of the HTTP header (e.g. "X-Custom-Auth")

value.description: Value is the value of the header

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Custom
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Custom is a credential that is set in a custom request header

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the header's Value

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Value
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Value is the value of the custom request header

clientID.description: ClientID sets the OAuth2 client ID

clientSecret.description: ClientSecret sets the OAuth2 client secret

tokenURL.description: TokenURL sets the token URL endpoint

scopes.description: Scopes is the list of OAuth2 scopes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: O Auth 2 Client Credentials
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: OAuth2ClientCredentials authenticates to the upstream via the standard OAuth2 client credentials flow

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the ClientSecret

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Client Secret
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: ClientSecret is the OAuth2 client secret

accessKeyID.description: AccessKeyID is the AWS access key ID

secretAccessKey.description: SecretAccessKey is the AWS secret access key

region.description: Region is the AWS region of the upstream API (e.g. "eu-central-1")

service.description: Service is the AWS service of the upstream API (e.g. "lambda", "s3")

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Sigv 4
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Sigv4 computes and injects AWS Signature Version 4 signatures on-the-fly for a Sigv4-compliant upstream API

fromSecret.description: FromSecret sets the name of the Secret whose value contains the SecretAccessKey

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Secret Access Key
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: SecretAccessKey is the AWS secret access key

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Mode is the expected format of the request body

maxRequestSize.description: MaxRequestSize sets the max body request byte size.

validation.description: Validation sets the validation of the request body content

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Body
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Body sets the request body-specific options. It requires enableRequestBuffering to be enabled.

jsonSchema.description: JSONSchema validates the request body against a JSON schema

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Validation
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Validation validates the content of the request body. A request whose body is invalid is rejected with a status code of `400`.

inline.description: Inline is the JSON schema itself

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: JSON Schema
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: JSONSchema validates the request body against a JSON schema

allowOriginStringMatch.description: AllowOriginStringMatch is the list of the allowed origins. An entry is either an exact origin (e.g. "https://example.com") or a `*` which allows every origin. A request whose Origin matches the Service's own origin is always allowed and it does not need to be listed here. Note that Octelium always responds with the request's own Origin rather than with a literal `*` since the browsers reject a wildcard whenever the request carries credentials.

allowMethods.description: AllowMethods specifies the content for the access-control-allow-methods header.

allowHeaders.description: AllowHeaders specifies the content for the access-control-allow-headers header.

exposeHeaders.description: ExposeHeaders specifies the content for the access-control-expose-headers header.

maxAge.description: MaxAge specifies the content for the access-control-max-age header.

allowCredentials.description: AllowCredentials specifies whether the resource allows credentials.

allowClusterServices.description: AllowClusterServices allows the origins of the Cluster's own Services (i.e. the Cluster domain itself as well as any of its subdomains at any depth, over HTTPS only) in addition to the origins that are set in `allowOriginStringMatch`. Credentials are always allowed for such origins regardless of `allowCredentials` since the Cluster's Services authenticate the browsers with the `octelium_auth` Cookie. This is needed to access the Service from the Cluster's own web console (e.g. the MCP and LLM playgrounds). Note that enabling this effectively trusts every Service in the Cluster since a browser-based application served by any of them can then read this Service's responses on behalf of the browsing User.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: CORS
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: CORS sets the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing options which are needed to access the Service from a browser-based application that is served at a different origin

addRequestHeaders.description: AddRequestHeaders is the list of request headers to be added.

removeRequestHeaders.description: RemoveRequestHeaders is the list of request headers to be removed.

addResponseHeaders.description: AddResponseHeaders is the list of response headers to be added.

removeResponseHeaders.description: RemoveResponseHeaders is the list of response headers to be removed.

forwardedMode.title: Forwarded Mode
forwardedMode.description: ForwardedMode sets how the `Forwarded` request header set by the downstream is handled

host.description: Host sets the Host request header forwarded to the upstream

authorizationMode.title: Authorization Mode
authorizationMode.description: AuthorizationMode sets how the downstream's `Authorization` request header is handled

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Header
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Header sets the manipulation of the request and response headers

preserve.description: Preserve preserves the Host header by using the Service's own FQDN as its value.

value.description: Value explicitly sets the Host header's value

eval.description: Eval sets the Host header's value to the result of a CEL expression that is evaluated against the request context.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Host
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Host sets the `Host` request header that is forwarded to the upstream. By default, the Host header is rewritten to the upstream's real host (i.e. the host of the Upstream's URL).

eval.description: Eval sets the header's value to the result of a CEL expression that is evaluated against the request context.

append.description: Append appends the header value instead of setting/overwriting/replacing it which is the default behavior.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key Value
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: KeyValue is a header that is added to the request or the response

addPrefix.description: AddPrefix adds a prefix to the request path.

removePrefix.description: RemovePrefix removes a prefix from the request path. You can use both RemovePrefix and AddPrefix at the same time to replace a prefix by another one.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Path
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Path sets the manipulation of the request path that is forwarded to the upstream

name.description: Name is the unique name of the Plugin

isDisabled.description: IsDisabled disables the Plugin without having to change its Condition or to delete it.

phase.title: Phase
phase.description: Phase sets whether the Plugin is invoked before or after the authentication and authorization processes

condition.description: Condition decides whether the Plugin is invoked on a per-request basis

extProc.description: ExtProc processes the requests via an Envoy ext_proc compliant gRPC server

lua.description: Lua processes the requests via a Lua script

direct.description: Direct returns a response directly without proxying the request to the upstream

jsonSchema.description: JSONSchema validates the JSON request body against a JSON schema

path.description: Path removes and/or adds prefixes of the request path

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Plugin
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Plugin provides a more advanced and dynamic way to manipulate the HTTP requests and responses. A Service can have one or more Plugins, including multiple Plugins of the same type.

key.description: Key sets the key of the cache entry

ttl.description: TTL is the duration after which a cache entry expires

maxSize.description: MaxSize is the maximum size in bytes of a response that can be cached

useXCacheHeader.description: UseXCacheHeader sets the `X-Cache` response header to indicate whether the response was served from the cache.

allowUnsafeMethods.description: AllowUnsafeMethods additionally caches the responses of the HTTP methods other than GET and HEAD which are the only cached methods by default.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Cache
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Cache returns globally cached responses that are stored in the Cluster's Redis store

eval.description: Eval sets the key to the result of a CEL expression that is evaluated against the request context.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Key is the key of the cache entry. By default, the request URI (i.e. the path and the query parameters) is used as the key on a per-Service basis.

statusCode.description: StatusCode is the status code of the returned response

body.description: Body is the body of the returned response

headers.description: Headers is the list of the headers that are set in the returned response

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Direct
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Direct returns a response directly without proxying the request to the upstream

inline.description: Inline is the response body as a string

inlineBytes.description: InlineBytes is the response body as raw bytes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Body
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Body is the body of the returned response

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key Value
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: KeyValue is a header that is set in the returned response

address.description: Address is the address of the ext_proc gRPC server (e.g. "ext-proc.default.svc:8080")

container.description: Container serves the ext_proc gRPC server from a managed container

processingMode.description: ProcessingMode sets which parts of the request and the response are sent to the ext_proc server

messageTimeout.description: MessageTimeout is the duration after which a message sent to the ext_proc server times out

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Ext Proc
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: ExtProc processes the requests via an external gRPC server that is compliant with Envoy's ext_proc protocol. Vigil acts as the ext_proc gRPC client that sends a ProcessingRequest and waits for a ProcessingResponse on every request.

image.description: Image is the image URL of the container

port.description: Port is the port at which the ext_proc gRPC server listens

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Container
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Container is a managed container that serves the ext_proc gRPC server

requestHeaderMode.title: Header Send Mode
requestHeaderMode.description: HeaderSendMode sets whether the headers are sent to the ext_proc server

responseHeaderMode.title: Header Send Mode
responseHeaderMode.description: HeaderSendMode sets whether the headers are sent to the ext_proc server

requestBodyMode.title: Body Send Mode
requestBodyMode.description: BodySendMode sets whether the body is sent to the ext_proc server

responseBodyMode.title: Body Send Mode
responseBodyMode.description: BodySendMode sets whether the body is sent to the ext_proc server

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Processing Mode
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: ProcessingMode sets which parts of the request and the response are sent to the ext_proc server

inline.description: Inline is the JSON schema itself

statusCode.description: StatusCode is the status code that is returned once the validation fails

body.description: Body is the body of the response that is returned once the validation fails

headers.description: Headers is the list of the headers that are set in the response that is returned once the validation fails

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: JSON Schema
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: JSONSchema validates the JSON request body against a JSON schema

inline.description: Inline is the response body as a string

inlineBytes.description: InlineBytes is the response body as raw bytes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Body
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Body is the body of the response that is returned once the validation fails

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key Value
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: KeyValue is a header that is set in the returned response

inline.description: Inline is the Lua script itself

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Lua
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Lua invokes a Lua script that can define an `onRequest` function which is invoked upon receiving the request before proxying it to the upstream, and an `onResponse` function which is invoked upon receiving the response from the upstream. A function that is not defined is silently skipped.

addPrefix.description: AddPrefix adds a prefix to the request path.

removePrefix.description: RemovePrefix removes a prefix from the request path. You can use both RemovePrefix and AddPrefix at the same time to replace a prefix by another one.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Path removes and/or adds prefixes of the request path

statusCode.description: StatusCode is the status code that is returned once the rate limit is exceeded. It is 429 by default.

body.description: Body is the body of the response that is returned once the rate limit is exceeded

key.description: Key sets the key by which the requests are counted

limit.description: Limit is the maximum number of requests that are allowed within the window

window.description: Window is the duration of the sliding window

headers.description: Headers is the list of the headers that are set in the response that is returned once the rate limit is exceeded

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Rate Limit
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: RateLimit provides a global sliding-window rate limiting mechanism that is backed by the Cluster's Redis store

inline.description: Inline is the response body as a string

inlineBytes.description: InlineBytes is the response body as raw bytes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Body
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Body is the body of the response that is returned once the rate limit is exceeded

eval.description: Eval sets the key to the result of a CEL expression that is evaluated against the request context.

perUser.description: PerUser applies the rate limit on a per-User basis

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Key is the key by which the requests are counted. By default, the rate limit is applied on a per-Session basis.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Key Value
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: KeyValue is a header that is set in the returned response

direct.description: Direct returns a response directly without proxying the request to the upstream

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Response
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Response sets the response-specific configuration

statusCode.description: StatusCode is the status code of the returned response

contentType.description: ContentType is the value of the `Content-Type` response header (e.g. "image/png")

inline.description: Inline is the response body as a string

inlineBytes.description: InlineBytes is the response body as raw bytes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Direct
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Direct returns a response directly from the Service without proxying the request to the upstream

maxRetries.description: MaxRetries is the maximum number of retries

initialInterval.description: InitialInterval is the duration of the backoff before the first retry

maxInterval.description: MaxInterval is the upper bound of the backoff duration between the retries

maxElapsedTime.description: MaxElapsedTime is the deadline after which no further retries are performed

multiplier.description: Multiplier is the floating point value by which the backoff duration is multiplied on each retry

statusCodes.description: StatusCodes is the list of the response status codes that are retried. By default, the Service currently retries on the 502, 503 and 504 status codes.

retryOnServerErrors.description: RetryOnServerErrors additionally retries on every 5xx response status code.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Retry
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Retry sets the retrying of the failed upstream requests. Retrying is disabled by default. The Service uses an exponential backoff that starts with the initialInterval duration which is multiplied on each retry by the multiplier until it reaches the maxInterval duration.

enableRequestBodyMap.description: Capture the request body map, currently JSON

enableResponseBodyMap.description: Capture the response body map, currently JSON

includeRequestHeaders.description: IncludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeResponseHeaders.description: IncludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeAllRequestHeaders.description: IncludeAllRequestHeaders records every request header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeRequestHeaders.

includeAllResponseHeaders.description: IncludeAllResponseHeaders records every response header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeResponseHeaders.

excludeRequestHeaders.description: ExcludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

excludeResponseHeaders.description: ExcludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Visibility
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Visibility sets the HTTP-specific access logging configuration

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: Protocol is the inference API protocol served by the Service.

model.description: Model overwrites the model name requested by the downstream before the request is proxied to the upstream. If not set, which is the default, the requested model name is preserved as is. Note that the model access control itself is done by the Policies via the `ctx.request.llm.model` field which always carries the model name as requested by the downstream.

limits.description: Limits sets the request parsing and semantic limits. These fields have to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

auth.description: Auth sets authentication-to-upstream specific configuration. This is where the upstream provider credentials (e.g. the OpenAI API key as a bearer token or the Anthropic API key as the `x-api-key` custom header) are set. Octelium never forwards the downstream credentials to the upstream provider.

header.description: Header sets request and response header manipulation options

path.description: Path sets the upstream request path options

plugins.description: Plugins is the list of plugins. The Cache plugin is unsupported for LLM Services since generic HTTP caching understands neither the authorization scope nor the model, tool and sampling parameters that make up a correct inference cache key.

isUpstreamHTTP2.description: IsUpstreamHTTP2 sets HTTP connections to the upstream to HTTP/2. Not enabled by default.

listenHTTP2.description: ListenHTTP2 sets the Service to listen to HTTP 2.0 connections. This is only enabled by default for Services using TLS. This field has to be enabled in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

visibility.description: Visibility sets the visibility/access logging specific options

cors.description: CORS sets the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing options which are needed to access the Service from a browser-based application served at a different origin (e.g. the Cluster's own web dashboard). This field has to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work since the CORS preflight requests carry no identity.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: LLM
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: LLM sets the LLM-gateway-specific configuration. LLM Services are HTTP-based: they reuse the entire HTTP dataplane and additionally understand the inference API semantics.

maxRequestBytes.description: MaxRequestBytes is the maximum size in bytes of the request body that is buffered and parsed. Zero uses the default value. This value is always bounded by an internal hard limit.

maxStreamEventBytes.description: MaxStreamEventBytes is the maximum size in bytes of a single `text/event-stream` response event that is parsed. Larger events are still forwarded to the downstream as is, they are simply not inspected. Zero uses the default value.

maxEstimatedInputTokens.description: MaxEstimatedInputTokens rejects the requests whose pre-flight estimated input token count is above this value. Note that this count is a byte-based heuristic calculated by Octelium itself, it is neither a provider-accurate token count nor an upper bound of one. Read the `ctx.request.llm.estimateQuality` field to know whether the estimate accounted for the entire input. Use the MaxRequestBytes field whenever an exact ceiling is needed.

maxOutputTokens.description: MaxOutputTokens rejects the requests whose own requested maximum output token count is above this value.

maxTools.description: MaxTools rejects the requests that declare more tools than this value.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Limits
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Limits sets the LLM request parsing and inference limits

value.description: Value overwrites the model name requested by the downstream with a static one.

eval.description: Eval overwrites the model name requested by the downstream with the result of a CEL expression that is evaluated against the request context. An empty result preserves the requested model name.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Model
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Model overwrites the model name requested by the downstream

enableRequestBody.description: EnableRequestBody records the request body, which contains the prompt, in the AccessLogs. It is disabled by default since the prompts are far more sensitive than typical HTTP request bodies: they routinely contain secrets, PII, source code and proprietary data.

enableRequestBodyMap.description: EnableRequestBodyMap records the serialized request body in the AccessLogs. It is disabled by default for the same reason.

enableResponseBody.description: EnableResponseBody records the response body, which contains the generated completion, in the AccessLogs. It is disabled by default. Note that it is only recorded for the responses that are not streamed.

enableResponseBodyMap.description: EnableResponseBodyMap records the serialized response body in the AccessLogs. It is disabled by default.

includeRequestHeaders.description: IncludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeResponseHeaders.description: IncludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeAllRequestHeaders.description: IncludeAllRequestHeaders records every request header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeRequestHeaders.

includeAllResponseHeaders.description: IncludeAllResponseHeaders records every response header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeResponseHeaders.

excludeRequestHeaders.description: ExcludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

excludeResponseHeaders.description: ExcludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Visibility
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Visibility sets the LLM-specific access logging configuration

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the canonical MCP endpoint path (e.g. `/mcp`) that is served to the downstreams. Any request whose path does not exactly match it is rejected. If not set, which is the default, every request path is accepted. Note that this field validates the downstream request path, it does not set the upstream one. Since MCP is a single endpoint protocol, the path of the upstream URL entirely replaces the request path that is proxied to the upstream. For instance, an upstream URL of `https://example.com/api/mcp` proxies every request to `/api/mcp` regardless of the downstream path. This is needed since many MCP servers are served at a path that differs from the one that the Service serves to its downstreams. Whenever the upstream URL carries no path at all, which is the default, the downstream request path is proxied to the upstream as is. This is needed since many MCP servers are served at the root path. This field has to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

protocol.description: Protocol sets the MCP protocol validation options. These fields have to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

limits.description: Limits sets the MCP request parsing limits. These fields have to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

header.description: Header sets request and response header manipulation options. Note that the MCP reserved headers (i.e. `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` and `Mcp-Param-*`) can be manipulated here too. Octelium never uses them to make authorization decisions, which are always made from the JSON-RPC request body itself, however the upstream MCP server rejects the requests whose headers do not match the body.

path.description: Path sets the upstream request path options

plugins.description: Plugins is the list of plugins. The Cache plugin is unsupported for MCP Services since generic HTTP caching understands neither the authorization scope nor the MCP cache invalidation semantics. Note that a Plugin that rewrites the JSON-RPC request body (e.g. Lua, ExtProc) should also rewrite the corresponding MCP reserved headers whenever the downstream sets them, otherwise the upstream MCP server rejects the request since the headers no longer match the body.

isUpstreamHTTP2.description: IsUpstreamHTTP2 sets HTTP connections to the upstream to HTTP/2. Not enabled by default.

listenHTTP2.description: ListenHTTP2 sets the Service to listen to HTTP 2.0 connections. This is only enabled by default for Services using TLS. This field has to be enabled in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

visibility.description: Visibility sets the visibility/access logging specific options

cors.description: CORS sets the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing options which are needed to access the Service from a browser-based application served at a different origin (e.g. the Cluster's own web dashboard). An Origin that is allowed here is also accepted by the Origin request header validation. This field has to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work since the CORS preflight requests carry no identity.

disableOriginCheck.description: DisableOriginCheck disables the `Origin` request header validation entirely. The validation rejects any request whose Origin is neither the Service's own origin nor an origin that is allowed by the `cors` field. Requests that carry no Origin request header at all, which is the case for nearly every non-browser MCP client (e.g. IDEs, AI agents, CLI tools), are always accepted. This field has to be set in the "default" or global Configuration (as opposed to named dynamic Configs) in order to actually work.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: MCP
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: MCP sets the Model Context Protocol-specific configuration. MCP Services are HTTP-based: they reuse the entire HTTP dataplane and additionally understand the MCP JSON-RPC semantics.

maxRequestBytes.description: MaxRequestBytes is the maximum size in bytes of the JSON-RPC request body that is buffered and parsed. Zero uses the default value. This value is always bounded by an internal hard limit.

maxStreamEventBytes.description: MaxStreamEventBytes is the maximum size in bytes of a single `text/event-stream` response event that is parsed. Larger events are still forwarded to the downstream as is, they are simply not inspected. Zero uses the default value.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Limits
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Limits sets the MCP request parsing limits

versions.description: Versions is an optional allowlist of the accepted MCP protocol versions (e.g. "2026-07-28"). If not set, which is the default, every version is accepted. Octelium does not maintain its own set of supported MCP protocol versions.

requireVersion.description: RequireVersion rejects the requests that do not declare a protocol version in either the `MCP-Protocol-Version` request header or the request body's `_meta` field. It is disabled by default since the header was only introduced in the 2025-06-18 revision.

rejectUnknownMethods.description: RejectUnknownMethods rejects any JSON-RPC method that is unknown to Octelium. It is disabled by default. Keeping it disabled lets the official MCP extensions as well as the newer protocol revisions reach the upstream while still being visible to Policies via the `ctx.request.mcp.method` field.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Protocol
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Protocol sets the MCP protocol validation options

disableRequestBody.description: DisableRequestBody disables recording the JSON-RPC request body in the AccessLogs. The request body is recorded by default since inspecting the MCP request is the whole point of using MCP mode as opposed to HTTP mode.

disableResponseBody.description: DisableResponseBody disables recording the JSON-RPC response body, which includes the individual `text/event-stream` response events, in the AccessLogs. The response body is recorded by default.

includeRequestHeaders.description: IncludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeResponseHeaders.description: IncludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are recorded in the AccessLogs.

includeAllRequestHeaders.description: IncludeAllRequestHeaders records every request header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeRequestHeaders.

includeAllResponseHeaders.description: IncludeAllResponseHeaders records every response header in the AccessLogs except for the ones set in excludeResponseHeaders.

excludeRequestHeaders.description: ExcludeRequestHeaders is the list of the request headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

excludeResponseHeaders.description: ExcludeResponseHeaders is the list of the response headers that are never recorded in the AccessLogs.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: SecurityContext sets the security-related configuration of the managed container

add.description: Add is the list of the added Linux capabilities (e.g. "NET_ADMIN", "SYS_TIME")

drop.description: Drop is the list of the dropped Linux capabilities (e.g. "ALL")

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Capabilities
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Capabilities sets the Linux capabilities of the managed container

name.description: Name is the name of the Volume. It is used by the VolumeMounts to reference the Volume.

persistentVolumeClaim.description: PersistentVolumeClaim uses a Kubernetes persistent volume claim as the Volume

emptyDir.description: EmptyDir uses a Kubernetes emptyDir as the Volume

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Volume
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Volume is a Kubernetes volume that is defined for the managed container

sizeLimitMegabytes.description: SizeLimitMegabytes is the size limit of the volume in megabytes

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Empty Dir
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: EmptyDir is a Kubernetes emptyDir volume

name.description: Name is the name of the Kubernetes persistent volume claim

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Persistent Volume Claim
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: PersistentVolumeClaim is a Kubernetes persistent volume claim

name.description: Name is the name of the mounted Volume

mountPath.description: MountPath is the path inside the container at which the Volume is mounted

subPath.description: SubPath is the path within the Volume that is mounted instead of its root

readOnly.description: ReadOnly mounts the Volume as read-only

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Volume Mount
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: VolumeMount mounts a defined Volume inside the managed container

endpoints.description: Endpoints is the list of endpoints

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Loadbalance
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Loadbalance is the list of upstreams to load balance among. Random load balancing is currently automatically enforced among the different endpoints.

url.description: URL is the canonical URL of the upstream. Examples are `http://example.com`, `postgres://pg.default.svc`, `tcp://my-custom-app:9090`,  and `https://api.sandbox.paypal.com`.

user.description: User is the User name if the upstream should be served by an active Connection of a User. If set, that means that the Service is served by any connected client owned by that User and willing to serve the Service.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.title: Endpoint
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.C.description: Endpoint is a single upstream endpoint

replicas.description: Replicas sets the number of replicas of a deployed Service.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.title: Deployment
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.description: Deployment sets the configuration of the Kubernetes deployment implementing the Service

configs.description: Configs is the list of named configurations that will override the global/default Service configuration if a rule matches.

rules.description: Rules is the list of rules that are checked on a per-request basis, if a rule matches its named configuration is used as the Service configuration for that specific request.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.title: Dynamic Config
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.description: DynamicConfig overrides the global/static Service Config on a per-request basis. If no Rule matches, the global Config is used as a fallback.

configName.description: configName is the name of the namedConfig that is used if the rule matches.

eval.description: Eval is the CEL expression that evaluates the Service config

opa.description: OPA is the Rego OPA script that evaluates the Service config

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.title: Rule
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Spec.D.description: Rule is evaluated on a per-request basis to choose or generate the Config used for that specific request

addresses.description: Addresses is the list of private addresses used by the Service for client-based connections.

namespaceRef.description: NamespaceRef is the reference of the owner Namespace

managedService.description: ManagedService is the configuration of the Service if it is deployed and maintained by the Cluster itself.

regionRef.description: RegionRef is the reference of the Region in which the Service is deployed.

primaryHostname.description: PrimaryHostname is the Service's primary hostname

additionalHostnames.description: AdditionalHostnames is the list of the Service's additional hostnames

port.description: Port is the port number used by the Service's listener

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: Status
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: Status is the current status of the Service

dualStackIP.description: DualStackIP is the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of the Service

podRef.description: PodRef is the reference of the Pod serving the Service

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: Address
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: Address is a private address at which the Service is reachable by the Cluster's clients

image.description: Image is the image URL of the managed Service's container

port.description: Port is the port exposed by the managed Service's container

hasSubdomain.description: HasSubdomain determines whether the managed Service additionally serves the subdomains of its FQDNs.

forwardHost.description: ForwardHost determines whether the downstream Host header is forwarded to the managed Service as is.

type.description: Type is the type of the managed Service

k8sLabels.description: K8sLabels is the map of the additional Kubernetes labels set for the managed Service's Kubernetes resources.

command.description: Command overrides the container image's command

args.description: Args is the list of command arguments that override the image arguments

imagePullSecret.description: ImagePullSecret is the name of the Kubernetes secret used to pull the container image from a private registry.

healthCheck.description: HealthCheck sets the health check of the managed Service

resourceLimit.description: ResourceLimit sets the managed Service's container resource limits

readOnlyFileSystem.description: ReadOnlyFileSystem sets the container's root filesystem to read-only

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: Managed Service
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: ManagedService is the configuration of a Service that is deployed and maintained by the Cluster itself (e.g. the built-in Services of the Cluster such as the AuthService and the Portal)

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: Health Check
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: HealthCheck is the health check used by the Cluster to probe the managed Service

port.description: Port is the port at which the health check is served

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: GRPC
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: GRPC is a gRPC health check

octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.title: Resource Limit
octelium.api.main.core.v1.Service.Status.description: ResourceLimit sets the compute resource limits of the managed Service

millicores.description: Millicores is the integer that sets the limit milli-cores

megabytes.description: Megabytes is the integer that sets the limit in megabytes

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.DualStackIP.title: Dual Stack IP
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.DualStackIP.description: DualStackIP is a pair of an IPv4 and an IPv6 address.

milliseconds.description: Milliseconds is the duration set in milliseconds

seconds.description: Seconds is the duration set in seconds

minutes.description: Minutes is the duration set in minutes

hours.description: Hours is the duration set in hours

days.description: Days is the duration set in days

weeks.description: Weeks is the duration set in weeks

months.description: Months is the duration set in months

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Duration.title: Duration
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Duration.description: Duration is a length of time that is expressed in a single unit of choice. Exactly one of the units is set (e.g. `seconds: 30`).

uid.description: UID is the unique UUID value for the object assigned by the Cluster. Read-only.

name.description: Name is the name of the object. It must be unique within a certain API/Version/Kind tuple.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the timestamp of creation of the object. Read-only.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the timestamp of when the object was last updated. Read-only.

displayName.description: DisplayName is the name that can be shown publicly for the object. Doesn't need to be unique.

description.description: Description is used to describe the object in a short sentence. Maximum characters are 1000.

labels.description: Labels is a map of string keys and values to organize objects.

tags.description: Tags is an optional array of tags that classify the Resource.

annotations.description: Annotations is a map of string keys and values that can be used to store arbitrary metadata about the object.

picURL.description: PicURL is the Picture URL of the resource.

resourceVersion.description: ResourceVersion is a unique ID that represent the current version of the resource object. Used by the Cluster to detect updates.

lastResourceVersion.description: LastResourceVersion is the ResourceVersion of the last update of the Resource.

actorRef.description: ActorRef is the object reference to the Actor resource, typically a Session, who is responsible for the current resource change. If ActorRef is not set, then the current change of the resource was done by the Cluster

actorOperation.description: ActorOperation is the gRPC full method triggered by the actorRef to modify the Resource

isSystem.description: IsSystem means that the resource is created by the Cluster and it cannot be managed by the administrators. Read-only.

specLabels.description: SpecLabels is map used internally by the Cluster for quick searches among lists of objects. Read-only.

isUserHidden.description: IsUserHidden means that the resource object is hidden from ordinary Users and should not be exposed via the User APIs.

isSystemHidden.description: IsSystemHidden means that the resource object is hidden by the Cluster and should not be exposed via the APIs.

systemLabels.description: SystemLabels is a similar map to specLabels. Used only by the Cluster.

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Metadata.title: Metadata
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Metadata.description: Metadata is the metadata that is common to every Cluster resource. It carries the resource's identity (i.e. its UID and name), its human-readable information as well as the Cluster-managed bookkeeping of the resource's versioning and provenance.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion is the API version of the reference resource

kind.description: Kind is the resource kind. A kind is unique per an APIVersion.

uid.description: UID is the resource object UID. A UID is unique across the entire Cluster.

name.description: Name is the resource object name. A name is unique per a certain kind.

resourceVersion.description: ResourceVersion is the resourceVersion of the resource.

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.ObjectReferenc.title: Object Reference
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.ObjectReferenc.description: ObjectReference is a reference to another Cluster resource. It identifies the referenced resource by its kind and either its UID or its name.
